claims.text: The as-manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a homogeneous FCC matrix.
The as-manufactured alloy has a relatively uniform grain structure.
The as-manufactured alloy lacks pre-existing oxide scales.
The as-manufactured alloy lacks significant grain-boundary segregation.
Elevated-temperature degradation is primarily governed by gas-environment-mediated grain-boundary processes.
Oxidizing exposure produces a partially protective but non-uniform surface oxide scale.
Oxide-scale formation locally depletes chromium and titanium at grain boundaries.
Chromium and titanium depletion undermines grain-boundary mechanical integrity.
A strongly reducing atmosphere prevents formation or retention of a stable protective oxide scale.
The absence of a stable oxide scale directly exposes grain boundaries to the reducing environment.
Direct grain-boundary exposure in reducing gas accelerates intergranular degradation and crack nucleation.
Loss of grain-interface cohesion can cause catastrophic failure through intergranular cracking.
Oxidizing exposure will produce pronounced grain-boundary elemental depletion.
Oxidizing exposure will produce minor intergranular crack initiation.
Reducing exposure will produce significant intergranular attack with widespread cracking and failure.
Inert-atmosphere exposure at the same temperatures will cause minimal degradation.
Oxidizing and reducing exposures will produce degradation patterns distinct from the inert-atmosphere baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies between approximately 600 and 800 degrees Celsius under strongly oxidizing or strongly reducing gas atmospheres.
